name: Fügen
kurzbeschreibung: Experience an active holiday in the Zillertal Valley, with the Spieljoch mountain cable car and Europe’s largest artificial white-water canal.
beschreibung:
Overview

Fügen is situated at an elevation of 545 meters at the entrance to the Zillertal valley in the district of Schwaz, framed by the Tux Prealps to the west and the Kitzbühel Alps to the east. With approximately 4,300 residents, Fügen is the most populous municipality and the economic and cultural center of the lower Zillertal, anchoring the Erste Ferienregion im Zillertal. This heritage-rich market town seamlessly unites premier alpine holiday infrastructure with vibrant Tyrolean traditions. From family skiing on Mount Spieljoch and year-round aquatic wellness at the Erlebnistherme Zillertal to exploring the global propagation of the Christmas carol Silent Night, Fügen provides an extraordinarily multifaceted holiday experience.

History

Settlement in the valley dates back to the Bronze Age, as evidenced by an urnfield cemetery dating from the twelfth century BC. Fügen was first documented in written records around 1130 under the name Fugine in episcopal registers of Brixen. From the fifteenth century onward, Fügen flourished as a prominent center of Tyrolean metallurgy: iron and copper ores were extracted in the Öxltal valley, and seventeenth-century forge mills produced cannonballs for regional defense. A historic milestone occurred in 1822 at Fügen Castle (Bubenburg), when Emperor Francis I of Austria and Tsar Alexander I of Russia were hosted, listening to local folk singers. Fügen achieved worldwide historical renown as the launchpad for the carol Silent Night, Holy Night: in 1819, master organ builder Carl Mauracher brought a handwritten musical transcript from Oberndorf near Salzburg to Fügen, where it was performed in the Gothic parish church of the Assumption. The famous Rainer Singers from Fügen subsequently toured Europe, introducing the carol to King George IV in London in 1827 and performing it in New York in 1839, marking its American debut. Today, the Fügen Heritage Museum in the historic Widumspfiste houses the world's most extensive documentation on the carol's global dissemination.

Getting There

By automobile, motorists take the Inntal motorway A12 to the Wiesing/Zillertal exit, following the well-developed B169 Zillertal highway for approximately ten minutes directly into Fügen. Rail travelers arrive via international Railjet and ICE express lines at the Jenbach transport hub. Directly from the adjacent platform, visitors transfer to the narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn railway, which operates every half hour, reaching Fügen-Hart station in just fifteen minutes; nostalgic steam trains operate in summer. Locally, regional bus line 8330 and a comprehensive network of complimentary ski and hiking buses connect all village quarters and base terminals.

Tips

The state-of-the-art Spieljochbahn gondola whisks guests directly from the village up to the family adventure peak Mount Spieljoch at 1,865 meters, home to climbing crags, mountain lakes, and the historic Öxltal Show Mine—the highest accessible underground mine in Austria. In winter, the Spieljoch ski area offers 21 kilometers of pistes alongside the valley's longest snowmaking-equipped descent (5.5 km). Pure wellness awaits at Erlebnistherme Zillertal, boasting outdoor thermal brine pools, sauna complexes, and the thrilling 133-meter Black Hole water slide. Cultural enthusiasts must tour the Widumspfiste museum to discover the Silent Night collection and stroll across the historic courtyard of Fügen Castle.
